M CHARACTER DOSSIER · SOLSTICE
Marasa'n
Neakia
The Last Even Daughter of Adonai-Vel
AGE716, by her own count
SPECIESNephilim (Balanced)
ORIGINAdonai-Vel, the Seat Between
OCCUPATIONFreelance mercenary
FACTIONUnaffiliated
CALLSIGN"The Old Hand"

"I've buried a nation and outlived the people who forgot it happened. A bar fight isn't going to be what does it."

SECTION 02

Appearance

There's a stillness to her that people clock before they can explain it, a symmetry that sits slightly too exact, a calm that sits slightly too complete. Centuries do that to a face. She stands tall, built more for endurance and power than speed, with the kind of quiet physical presence that makes a crowded room rearrange itself around her without anyone quite deciding to.

Distinguishing features

Heterochromia is the tell she spends the most effort hiding: one eye a warm gold amber, the other a deep, star flecked black. Pale seam-like markings run along her collarbone and spine, old scar-pale lines where the two halves of her blood never quite finished sealing shut. She carries the ghost of wings at her shoulder blades too, just ridges now, tender to the touch and impossible to explain if anyone ever sees them.

Armour and equipment

Deep blue and gold plate, old-world craftsmanship gone soft at the edges from centuries of actual use rather than display. A heavy hood, worn up more often than not, with long silver-white hair falling forward over one eye, an old habit that hides her heterochromia without ever looking deliberate. She fights with a greatsword she's carried longer than most nations last, its blade cold-forged in a style no living smith would recognise.

Origins of the blade

Clear Light and Pure Darkness is older than she is by roughly three centuries, forged in Adonai-Vel while the Seat Between was still whole, long before the slow decline she was actually born into. Old family telling credits the work to an order the records simply call the Twinsmiths, forge-masters who worked in pairs, one attuned to Aurelia's warmth and one to Nyxtra's quiet, striking the same length of steel from opposite ends of belief until it held both at once. It was not a common commission even then. A blade that could carry two opposing resonances without one eventually smothering the other took a forge, a technique, and a kind of patience that only existed in a nation built on proving the same thing was possible in flesh and blood.

Nobody living knows how it was actually done. The Twinsmiths' order died with the rest of Adonai-Vel, and whatever method let their forges hold both resonances steady in the same steel went with them, not even fragments of it survive in the Aetherforge Guild's records, which is the closest thing the modern world has to an authority on working Solethium and old metallurgy alike. It means the blade cannot be repaired the way an ordinary sword could. If it ever truly breaks, it stays broken.

It came to her the way most things worth keeping did, through her father, who trained her with it before it was ever meant to be hers. She had it with her on the errand that kept her away from the capital the night of the Fracturing, which makes it one of a literal handful of confirmed objects left anywhere in the world that came out of Adonai-Vel whole. A thousand years on, it has not dulled the way ordinary steel would, and it has never once needed reforging. Nobody left alive can tell her why, only that it is one more thing about her inheritance nobody can fully explain anymore.

She cleans it the same exact way after every fight for exactly this reason. It is not superstition, or not only superstition. It is the only maintenance a blade like this will ever get again.

Powers and abilities

She is not a spellcaster in the way most people picture one. No spell list, no utility magic, no illusions or summons. What she has instead runs through only two channels, her own body and the blade in her hands, both drawing from the same well rather than a wide spread of separate tricks. As a balanced Nephilim, she draws on both light and shadow without the resistance most casters feel picking a side, though she will never go as deep into either school as a dedicated specialist would. She is also naturally resistant to charm, fear, and possession, a side effect of a mind built to hold two opposing forces steady without breaking.

Her first technique is the Surge. In the half-second before a strike lands, she pushes both halves of her inheritance into her own body at once, gold warmth and star black together, physically amplifying the blow past what her frame should be capable of, hard enough to crack stone or bone outright. Her collarbone and spine markings catch light and shadow at the same instant, then fade.

The same charge can be poured into Clear Light and Pure Darkness instead of her own body. Channeled into the steel, the blade stops behaving like ordinary metal, one edge running hot enough to sear through wards or unnatural growth, the other running cold and quiet enough to unravel a lesser enchantment or numb a corrupted limb before it can react. Held long enough and released in one committed swing, that same charge can be thrown outward entirely, a visible arc of light and shadow tearing through the air well beyond the blade's actual reach. It is the closest thing she has to a ranged attack, and the most expensive thing she does. She saves it for fights that genuinely cannot be closed by hand.

Because she is genuinely balanced rather than leaning toward one court, her Fracture Sickness does not work the way it does for most of her kind. Where a leaning Nephilim tips further into whichever half already dominates, both of her halves destabilise at once, a far more violent and unpredictable break than a slow lean. Throwing the charge clear of the blade carries the same risk as the Surge, only more of it, which is part of why she rations both so carefully, and part of why Kell's Hollow frightened her so badly even after she pulled back from the edge of it.

The two reckonings

Everything above pulls on both halves at once, kept carefully in balance. There is one more thing she can do, and she does it as close to never as she can manage, because it means letting that balance go on purpose instead of holding it. Instead of keeping both halves paired, she can let just one run completely loose for a short stretch, closer to what her single-court cousins call their own magic, only far more of it, and far more dangerous to her than to anyone standing in front of her.

The Unbroken Dawn

She lets Aurelia's half run without restraint, gold light rising off her skin and the blade together, hot enough to purify or unmake. It can sear a clearing down to bare stone, unravel a standing working outright, or scour a Shardbeast's corruption before it has a chance to react. It doesn't care who else is standing nearby once it's loosed, which is most of why she treats it as an absolute last resort. It leaves her half blind for hours afterward and drives her hard toward the radiant edge of Fracture Sickness for as long as she holds it open. She has allowed herself this exactly four times in seven centuries.

The Hollow Quiet

The inverse, and just as dangerous. She lets Nyxtra's half run without restraint instead, and rather than a burst, the ground around her simply stops, sound gone, light gone, magic gone, a perfect dead quiet spreading outward that can unravel wards, smother a Shardbeast's frenzy into stillness, or erase every trace of a working that was ever cast there. She has used it to disappear as often as to fight. It leaves her freezing and unresponsive for long stretches afterward, and drives her hard toward the umbral edge of Fracture Sickness for as long as she holds it open.

Both are the same door, opened from opposite sides. She has never used them back to back, and has promised herself, quietly, that she never will.

CLEAR LIGHT · PURE DARKNESS

Off duty

The armour comes off and something older tends to surface. Hair worn loose, dark lipstick, black lace and old fine jewellery instead of plate. It's a face almost no one in her current life has actually seen.

In the Field

Armoured, hooded, unmistakably working.

Off Duty

Unarmoured, unguarded, rarely seen.

General impression: a woman who looks like she's stepped out of an old painting and is faintly annoyed about it. Striking without trying to be, and visibly unbothered by whether you notice.

SECTION 03

Personality

Centuries of watching empires rise and fall have flattened her capacity to be impressed by anything smaller than an apocalypse. She isn't cold, exactly. She's just run out of patience for pretending small things are large ones.

Strengths

  • Unshakeable under pressure, having genuinely seen worse
  • Centuries of honed instinct in a fight
  • Dry, exact honesty, she doesn't flatter and doesn't lie to make a moment easier
  • Quietly protective of people who've earned it, whether she admits to it or not

Flaws

  • Guards herself to a fault, even against people who deserve better
  • Reckless with her own safety in a way that reads as confidence but isn't
  • Struggles to let anyone stay close long enough to matter
  • Quietly punishes herself for things that were never her fault

Habits and quirks

She cleans her blade the exact same way after every fight, whether it needed one stroke or fifty. She counts under her breath in old Adonai-Vel numerals when she's impatient, a language nobody around her has heard in centuries. She pays every debt in exact coin and never haggles, a small, private superstition about owing anyone anything for longer than she has to.

Likes and dislikes

She likes quiet taverns off the main road, strong bitter drink, old maps, and good, honest craftsmanship, arcane or otherwise. She dislikes being thanked at length, crowds that press in too close, the wet heat of the Ember District, and people who ask about her past directly instead of letting her offer it.

Around others

Professionally courteous, dryly funny under stress, and very good at letting people believe whatever version of her keeps them both safe. She doesn't correct assumptions unless they're dangerous ones. She'll help without being asked twice and leave without being asked once.

SECTION 04

History

Her life reads less like a biography and more like a series of eras, most of which the rest of Solstice only knows as chapters in a history book.

  • THE OLD AGE · CHILDHOOD

    Born into a fading bridge

    She was born in Adonai-Vel long after the city's brightest years had already passed, in a household built on the exact premise the nation itself was founded on. Her father carried Aurelia's warmth in his blood, her mother carried Nyxtra's quiet, and neither parent ever treated the other's half as the lesser one. It was, by then, an increasingly rare kind of household to grow up in. The ceremonial schools that once trained children in both disciplines at once were closing faster than new ones could open, and by the time she was old enough to hold a blade, most of her education came from her parents directly rather than any hall of learning.

    Mornings belonged to her father and the sword. He drilled her in a cracked courtyard behind their home, the same forms his own father had taught him, footwork first, then weight, then the long patient work of turning a growing body into something that could actually carry a greatsword's mass. Evenings belonged to her mother and stillness, sitting at the edge of the old reflecting pools that still, somehow, held their shape even as the districts around them crumbled, learning to sit with the quieter half of her blood instead of flinching from it. She did not know, at the time, that she was being raised in the last house in the world still practising this particular kind of balance on purpose.

    She remembers the city itself only in fragments now, gold light catching dust in empty market squares, her mother's hand pulling her away from a sealed street, a name for a district that no longer means anything to anyone alive. She remembers being proud of her house's twin heritage, the way a child is proud of anything her parents seem unbothered by. She did not yet understand that pride was already an inheritance from a nation that no longer had the standing to hand it down.

  • THE FRACTURING

    The errand that saved her

    She was sent away from the capital on what her father called a training rite and what she, at the time, called an inconvenience, escorting a small supply cache to an outlying watch post three valleys east, a task usually given to soldiers twice her age. She argued to stay. She lost the argument. She left at dawn on foot with two older escorts and a complaint she never got to finish voicing, because that was the last ordinary morning her nation ever had.

    She felt it before she understood what she was feeling, a wrongness in the ground that reached her feet before any sound did, then the sky over the western ridge changing colour in a way sky is not supposed to change. She turned back toward the capital without waiting for her escorts to agree, and made it perhaps half a day before the first wave of fleeing people met her coming the other direction, moving faster than she was, moving away from the exact place she was trying to reach.

    She kept walking toward it for two more days anyway, past columns of smoke that did not behave like ordinary fire, past ground that had folded and risen in places that used to be flat, past people who could not answer her when she asked what was left standing. It took her that long, and the sight of the horizon where the capital's spires should have broken the skyline and did not, to finally accept there was nothing left to walk toward. She stood on a ridge overlooking what used to be her home and watched the sky above it stay the colour of a bruise for three full days, gold and black bleeding into each other with nowhere left to go, exactly the way the old stories now tell it, except she was actually there to see it happen.

  • THE FOUNDING YEARS

    A blade for a scattering of survivors

    What came after the Fracturing did not feel like a new beginning while she was living through it. It felt like drifting, one displaced column of survivors merging into another, no nation left to answer to and no clear direction to walk in beyond away from the worst of the wreckage. She fell in, eventually, with one of the larger refugee movements converging on a stretch of coast and highland that had somehow been spared the worst of the tearing, the same ground that would, in time, become Solstice.

    There was no city there yet, only tents, salvaged timber, and thousands of frightened people from a dozen dead or dying nations trying to work out how to survive the same winter together. Her blade stopped being a piece of family tradition almost overnight and became simply the most useful thing she owned. She escorted foraging parties into corrupted ground. She stood watch on the perimeter of camps that had no walls yet, only fear and exhaustion and whoever was still willing to hold a weapon through the night. Nobody asked where she'd trained or what her eyes meant under her hood. Everybody needed a blade, and she was very good at being one.

    She watched the first real walls go up around the settlement that would eventually take the name Solstice, watched the first arguments over what the new order should even look like, watched exhausted survivors from nations that used to distrust each other slowly agree to something like the Great Accord because the alternative was simply dying separately instead of surviving together. She did not participate in drafting any of it. She just kept the roads to it clear enough for other people to reach.

  • THE EMBER YEARS

    Guarding the first veins

    Decades into Solstice's slow climb out of its founding chaos, work took her south into the volcanic belt that would eventually become Vesprita, long before it had that name or the Aetherforge Guild had any formal claim over it. Independent prospecting crews were pushing into the mountainside after the first raw seams of Solethium, drawn by rumour and desperation in roughly equal measure, and none of them had any real idea yet what they were digging into. They needed blades who could handle both bandits and whatever occasionally crawled up out of the deeper shafts. She took the work because it paid and because, unlike most of the crews, she already understood exactly what kind of crystal they were pulling out of the ground.

    It was there, guarding a lantern-lit tunnel mouth on an unremarkable night, that she first watched her own blood answer a stray shard of exposed crystal, a thin, involuntary glow rising to the surface of a shallow cut before she'd even registered the wound. The old family caution about staying clear of raw Solethium stopped being inherited wisdom in that moment and became something she'd verified herself, in her own skin, by lamplight, with a prospecting crew none the wiser about what they'd just seen.

    She stayed in the region for years, long enough to watch the earliest scattered claims start organising into something more deliberate, the beginnings of the guild structure and shared safety practices that would eventually formalise into the Aetherforge Guild itself. She never joined it. She preferred contract work at the edges of it, close enough to the industry to understand it, far enough from its ledgers to stay unrecorded.

  • THE CONTAINMENT

    What she lost at Kell's Hollow

    Somewhere in those same Ember years she fell into partnership with a human mercenary named Corin Vasse, a partnership that lasted the better part of forty years, long enough that she stopped mentally preparing herself for the day she'd have to watch him age past her, the way she'd trained herself to do with every other close ally before him. He never asked what she was. He noticed, over the decades, and decided it changed nothing about the arrangement. It was the closest thing to family she had allowed herself since the Fracturing.

    The outbreak at Kell's Hollow started the way most Shardbeast incidents start, quietly, a missing miner, a strange growth reported and dismissed, a second disappearance that finally got taken seriously too late. By the time she and Corin were brought in with a small containment crew, the settlement's lower tunnels were already lost, and what came up out of them in the final hours of that job was faster and more numerous than anyone had prepared for.

    She does not describe, to anyone, exactly what happened in the tunnel collapse that took Corin. She describes only the aftermath, days afterward, alone in a supply tent, watching her own collarbone markings running hotter and colder than they should, her grief curdling into something that felt less like sorrow and more like her own two halves pulling in opposite directions for the first time in her long life. It was the closest she has ever personally come to Fracture Sickness, close enough that she still, centuries later, refuses to let any fight run a single moment longer than it strictly has to.

  • THE LONG PRESENT

    Centuries of contracts, one search underneath

    Everything since Kell's Hollow has followed roughly the same shape, one contract into the next, one city into the next, decades folding into each other with very little to mark where one ended and another began. She stopped forming partnerships the way she had with Corin. She took work instead, cleanly, professionally, and moved on before anyone could get close enough to become another name she'd have to carry.

    Somewhere in that long stretch of ordinary contract work, the other search kept running quietly underneath it, a name overheard in a Reach tavern, a folk tale that used the wrong words for the wrong things, a rumour worth three days' travel just to rule out. She found Ishvel'ta Corvain that way, decades ago, and later Doran'ai Fesk, then Vaeleth Orsimin, then eventually Tessari'yn Holt, each discovery feeling for a moment like the search was finally about to pay off, each one ultimately confirming instead that there was no hidden court left standing anywhere.

    She still takes contracts. She still moves through Solstice and the Reach the way she always has, professional, controlled, unremarkable until the exact moment she isn't. But somewhere in the last century, without ever announcing it to herself, the search for her people quietly became a search for proof instead, and she has been following that instead ever since.

Legends that have grown around her

The Even Hand

An old Reach story about a masked knight who settles debts of blood with perfect, unnerving fairness, never more violence than the situation calls for, never less. Nobody in the story is ever named. Reach elders tell it like a warning and a comfort in the same breath.

The Grey Halo

A mountain-pass folk tale about a hooded woman who once held a narrow crossing alone against a Shardbeast swarm until help arrived. Whether seeing her cloak in a dream means good luck or a warning depends entirely on which village you ask.

The Guild's Unpaid Debt

An old ledger entry in the Aetherforge Guild's records notes a masked contractor who resolved a catastrophic containment breach decades back and left before collecting full payment. Guild elders still raise a glass to "the contractor who's owed" on the anniversary, half-joking, half-not.

SECTION 05

Motivations

PRIMARY GOAL

Proof

Not rescue, not reunion. Just something real that outlives her, evidence that Adonai-Vel existed and mattered, in case she's the last thing that remembers it at all.

  • PERSONAL MOTIVATION

    She's stopped believing anyone else will do it

    She's met the other survivors. She knows now there's no hidden court left to find. If a record is going to exist, she's the one who has to make it happen, because there may not be anyone else left who still can.

  • FEAR

    Total erasure

    Not dying. She's made her peace with that centuries ago. What she's actually afraid of is dying with nothing left behind, the exact fate her nation already suffered, repeated one person smaller.

  • SECRET

    She could have made it back

    She has never told anyone that she was close enough, the night of the Fracturing, to have possibly reached the capital in time to die there with everyone else, or maybe even to warn them. She chose to finish the errand instead. She has spent seven centuries not looking directly at what that choice might have cost.

  • BREAKING POINT

    Watching it happen again

    Forced to stand by helplessly while a home, a family, or a community gets wiped out in front of her, the way hers was, is the one thing that could break her composure completely. Everything else she can absorb. Not that.

SECTION 06

Relationships

Ishvel'ta CorvainElder survivor
The oldest confirmed Nephilim survivor she's ever met, old enough to remember Adonai-Vel itself. Lives in near total isolation in Tenebrae's undercroft and refuses to discuss what she remembers.

An Aurelic-leaning Nephilim, younger than Marasa'n by at least a century, who still holds onto a hope Marasa'n gave up on. Their meetings, roughly once a decade, are never entirely comfortable.
Vaeleth OrsiminPeer, fixer
A retired Nyxtran mercenary who now runs a discreet information network out of Tenebrae. The closest thing she has to a peer rather than a stranger who happens to share her blood, and the likely source of her current lead.

The only other confirmed even-blooded Nephilim she's met. Chose total anonymity, farming quietly somewhere in the Reach under a name that isn't hers. Wants no part of searching or being found.
